Showcase the extent of ‘71 genocide
2022-04-01T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/showcase-the-extent-71-genocide-2995481

A preliminary survey of 34 districts found 14,452 incidents of genocide, 759 mass graves, 1,048 mass killing sites and 1,027 torture centres. Think about the figure we will get if we complete the survey in all 64 districts. I think the figure [of martyrs] will cross the margin of 30 lakh. Prof Muntassir Mamoon

A preliminary survey of 34 districts found 14,452 incidents of genocide, 759 mass graves, 1,048 mass killing sites and 1,027 torture centres. Think about the figure we will get if we complete the survey in all 64 districts. I think the figure [of martyrs] will cross the margin of 30 lakh.

Bangladesh needs to showcase the extent of genocide perpetrated by the Pakistan army during the Liberation War to expose the falseness of counter-narratives, researchers said yesterday.

They made the remarks while speaking at an international conference titled "Fifty Years' Journey of Bangladesh: Genocide, Nation-State and Bangabandhu's Cherished Bangladesh" at Bangla Academy.

The two-day conference has been organised by the 1971 Genocide-Torture Archive and Museum.

"The extent of the genocide was grave, but we could not showcase this with significance," said Liberation War Affairs Minister AKM Mozammel Haque.

"Our government is also trying to get international recognition of the genocide," he added.

Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies Director General Binayak Sen made the keynote presentation titled "Bangabandhu's Democratic Socialism".

"These works are needed as there are some other thoughts on 30 lakh martyrs in Bangladesh's Liberation War. We need to debunk that," said Indian journalist Manash Ghosh -- who covered the Liberation War on various battlefields -- referring to the museum's work.

He also mentioned that he was ashamed of Indian scholar Sarmila Bose, who in her book "Dead Reckoning: Memories of the 1971 Bangladesh War" claimed that 30 lakh people attaining martyrdom in the war of freedom was "baseless".

"It was a commissioned book," claimed Manosh, also writer of a book on the same war from his firsthand experiences.

Museum trustee, chair and historian Prof Muntassir Mamoon said, "If you do not talk about genocide and the torture of women, the discussions on the Liberation War will remain incomplete."

Prof Mamoon also mentioned that after a preliminary survey of 34 districts, the museum found 14,452 incidents of genocide, 759 mass graves, 1,048 mass killing sites and 1,027 torture centres.

"Think about the figure we will get if we complete the survey in all 64 districts. I think the figure will cross the margin of 30 lakh. Besides, five lakh additional people died at refugee camps," he added.

State minister for Cultural Affairs KM Khalid in his chief guest's speech echoed the same, mentioning how his upazila has 17 identified killing fields.

Lt Col (retd) Quazi Sajjad Ali Zahir Bir Pratik also spoke.
